html:
A Sudanese Sufi teacher who in 1881 declared himself the Mahdi, the redeemer Muslims expected before the end of time, and led a rising that drove Egyptian rule out of Sudan.

Sudan had been ruled from Cairo since the 1820s by the Khedivate of Egypt, whose taxes and foreign officials were hated. Muhammad Ahmad drew followers with a call to return to pure Islam. In 1883 his army destroyed an Egyptian force under the British officer William Hicks. In January 1885 it stormed Khartoum and killed the British general Charles Gordon, which caused an uproar in Britain.

He died a few months later, in June 1885, at Omdurman, probably of typhus. His successor, the Khalifa Abdallahi, ruled the Mahdist State until a British and Egyptian army crushed it at the Battle of Omdurman in 1898.
